_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for every threshold, band and weight in the SSB screening system.
Both the Python services and the React Native app read their values from this file:
Python  -> contracts/python/ssb_contracts/config.py (loads this file at import)
RN/TS   -> src/config/thresholds.ts (mirror, kept honest by __tests__/contracts.test.ts)
No component may define a threshold of its own. If a number below changes, bump
config_version and every consumer picks it up.
NONE OF THESE VALUES ARE SCIENTIFICALLY CALIBRATED FOR PRODUCTION USE.
Each carries its own provenance and confidence note. Read them before quoting a number.
Raw ArcFace R50 cosine similarity thresholds. The score is a cosine similarity in
[-1, 1], NOT a probability and NOT a percentage. Never rescale it for display.
similarity >= match           -> MATCH
review <= similarity < match  -> REVIEW
similarity <  review          -> NO_MATCH
face_verification.confidence: PROVISIONAL. Calibrated on LFW (same-domain photo pairs). Production use is cross-domain (document portrait vs live capture) and is NOT validated.

_comment: Applies to the DINOv2 tamper detection module. The real model does not exist yet;
these bands describe how a tamper_score in [0, 1] is banded once it does.
The mock emits scores consistent with these bands so the pipeline downstream of it
is exercised exactly as it will be in production.
document_forensics.confidence: PLACEHOLDER. No trained model exists. These bands must be re-derived from a validation set before the real DINOv2 head ships.

_comment: Evidence Fusion Engine. NOT LightGBM - this is deterministic weighted fusion.
risk_score is a normalised value in [0, 1]. It is a fused judgement, not a model
probability, and it is defined by this configuration rather than measured.
Weights apply only to modules that actually returned evidence. Modules that are
NOT_AVAILABLE or FAILED are dropped from the weighted mean and the remaining
weights are renormalised, so missing evidence never raises the score.
_minimum_evidence_weight_comment: The four core modules (forensics 0.40 + face 0.28 + validation 0.22 + ocr 0.06)
total 0.96. Requiring 0.90 therefore means: all four must have produced evidence
for a LOW clearance to stand, and only the anomaly gap (0.04, permanently
NOT_AVAILABLE while PatchCore is unimplemented) is tolerated.
This is the rule that stops a screening being cleared while the module that
would have caught the problem was down. A case where tamper detection never
ran is not a low-risk case; it is an unexamined one.

_comment: A strong single signal must not be diluted by other modules scoring low.
Each rule raises the FLOOR of the final band; none can lower it.
The REVIEW floors matter as much as the HIGH one: a module that says
'I cannot tell' must surface to the officer, not be averaged away by four
modules that had nothing to report.

risk_fusion.source: Weight ordering follows risk_Score/riskengine/risk.py (tampering 0.45 > face 0.30 > validation 0.25), extended to cover OCR and anomaly.
risk_fusion.confidence: PROVISIONAL. Weights are an engineering judgement about signal strength, not a fit to labelled fraud data. Do not present them as calibrated.

_comment: Mean per-field OCR recognition confidence, as reported by PP-OCRv5. Used only to
flag a weak read to the officer - it never decides anything on its own.
PatchCore is NOT IMPLEMENTED. No service produces this evidence. The block exists so
the threshold has a defined home the day the module lands; until then every anomaly
result is NOT_AVAILABLE and nothing reads these numbers.
anomaly.confidence: NOT IMPLEMENTED. PatchCore has not been built; no value has been derived.
